entries.name: Adventurers Guild Emblem
entries.summary: A polished guild emblem worn to identify the bearer as connected to an adventuring company or guild.

entries.name: Arena Mark
entries.summary: A marked token identifying the bearer as registered with an arena, fighting circuit, or controlled combat venue.

entries.name: Argent Heart
entries.summary: A dense, many-faceted core of rune-bound metal made to sit within the Founder's Hilt and regulate magical force through the restored blade. When carried close to the body, its measured pulse steadies circulating mana and gives subtle tactile warning of strain, turbulence, or disruption in nearby magical workings. It is a component of the weapon rather than a power source for Silvermaw Forge, grants no Arcana, and cannot function as a weapon by itself.

entries.name: Bloodoak Clan Signet Ring
entries.summary: A heavy signet ring bearing the carved symbol of the Bloodoak clan.

entries.name: Census Clerk Seal
entries.summary: A minor registry seal used by a census clerk for routine records and official verification.

entries.name: Founder's Sheath
entries.summary: An ancient black leather scabbard reinforced with engraved Argentsteel fittings and shaped for the Founder’s weapon. Its wolf-and-rune marks identify it as principal regalia of House Fenrisard-Argenwald and the Runed Argent Fang. When openly worn, it lends ceremonial weight to legitimate command and formal conduct, but possession alone does not grant title, office, obedience, or recognition.

entries.name: Hollowstar Clearance Band
entries.summary: A marked clearance band used at Hollowstar to show an approved level of access.

entries.name: Inquisitory Aide Badge
entries.summary: A badge identifying an aide, clerk, runner, or assistant attached to an inquisitorial office.

entries.name: Labor Tag
entries.summary: A stamped labor tag used to identify the bearer within an organized work crew or controlled labor system.

entries.name: Luporian Service Medallion
entries.summary: A small silver-gray medallion issued to formal household servants of House Luporian and intended to be worn while in service. Its face is smooth and blank before its enchantment first manifests, after which one of several traditional Luporian symbols appears and the medallion develops a corresponding magical property. Neither the wearer nor the household chooses which manifestation appears.

entries.name: Merchant House Signet
entries.summary: A signet linking the bearer to a merchant house and suitable for visible identification or sealing routine correspondence.

entries.name: Oathsun Ward Token
entries.summary: A token identifying the bearer as a ward, foundling, or recognized dependent of the Oathsun institution.

entries.name: Paladin's Silver Seal
entries.summary: A polished silver medallion bearing sacred and martial insignia associated with a paladin order.

entries.name: Seal of the Argent Fang
entries.summary: A heavy silver-gray signet ring bearing the rune-bound fang used to authenticate the lawful orders of the Runed Argent Fang’s commander. It is one part of the order’s command regalia and is used to seal formal instructions, appointments, and fortress instruments. Possession alone does not make the wearer First Fang and cannot replace the order’s recognition process.

entries.name: Tribunal Advocate Seal
entries.summary: A formal seal identifying an advocate, senior scribe, or authorized representative of a tribunal.

entries.name: Wand
entries.summary: A slender magical focus suited for quick gestures, precise channeling, and compact spellwork. A wand is light, portable, easy to conceal, and favored by casters who want their focus close at hand. It offers less stability than a staff, but more convenience.

entries.name: Warden's Chain
entries.summary: A linked ceremonial chain of dark steel and Argentsteel medallions, each engraved with a fortress, patrol charge, or defensive obligation once entrusted to the Runed Argent Fang. It represents responsibility for the order’s people, roads, wards, and strongholds rather than simple rank. The chain is worn during formal command rites but grants no authority to an unrecognized bearer.

entries.name: Worker's Badge
entries.summary: A simple stamped badge identifying the bearer with a recognized workshop, guild, factory, or work crew.

entries.name: Breastplate
entries.summary: A shaped metal breastplate with supporting padding and straps, protecting the torso while preserving more mobility than full plate.

entries.name: Chain Armor
entries.summary: A complete suit of mail over padded clothing, offering reliable battlefield protection at the cost of noise and weight.

entries.name: Chain Shirt
entries.summary: A lighter mail shirt with limited supporting protection, useful for travelers and guards who expect danger without wearing a full suit.

entries.name: Gambeson
entries.summary: A sturdy quilted gambeson that cushions impact and softens cuts, practical alone or beneath heavier armor.

entries.name: Half Plate
entries.summary: A serious partial plate harness combining metal plates, mail, straps, and padding while retaining more flexibility than full plate.

entries.name: Heavy Armor
entries.summary: A heavy frontline armor harness built to absorb dangerous blows and project martial presence, protective but tiring and conspicuous.

entries.name: Hide Armor
entries.summary: Rugged protection made from thick hides, layered leather, fur, bone, or similar natural materials common on dangerous frontiers.

entries.name: Leather Armor
entries.summary: A fitted suit of hardened and layered leather suited for scouts, hunters, guards, and adventurers who value mobility.

entries.name: Mage Ward Garments
entries.summary: Ward-treated spellcaster garments that offer modest physical protection while helping the wearer contain magical strain and circulating mana.

entries.name: Padded Armor
entries.summary: A humble suit of layered padded cloth, inexpensive and flexible but far better protection than ordinary clothing.

entries.name: Plate Armor
entries.summary: A full fitted harness of shaped plate, reinforced joints, straps, and padding, expensive and highly protective when properly worn.

entries.name: Reinforced Travel Gear
entries.summary: Durable travel clothing reinforced at vulnerable points with leather, heavy stitching, bracers, and practical road protection without becoming true armor.

entries.name: Scale Armor
entries.summary: Overlapping metal, horn, or hardened plates arranged like scales, providing solid protection while retaining useful flexibility.

entries.name: Stealth Armor
entries.summary: Dark flexible armor built to protect without clattering, flashing in low light, or badly restricting silent movement.

entries.name: Studded Leather Armor
entries.summary: Reinforced leather armor with hardened or metal-supported sections protecting vulnerable areas while remaining lighter than mail.

entries.name: Academy Uniform
entries.summary: A formal academy uniform of fitted student clothing and institutional insignia, suited to lessons, examinations, and supervised magical study.

entries.name: Artisan's Workwear
entries.summary: Practical workshop clothing built for tools, dust, splinters, stains, and long hours of skilled handwork.

entries.name: Cold Weather Cloak
entries.summary: A heavy weatherproof cloak made to trap warmth and shed snow during prolonged travel in freezing conditions.

entries.name: Cold Weather Outfit
entries.summary: Layered insulating clothing suited for snow, mountain cold, frozen roads, and long exposure to bitter wind.

entries.name: Commoner's Outfit
entries.summary: Plain, serviceable clothing of the sort worn by ordinary townsfolk, villagers, laborers, and travelers of modest means.

entries.name: Courtier's Attire
entries.summary: Polished formal clothing cut for audiences, negotiations, court halls, and rooms where appearance and etiquette are closely judged.

entries.name: Desert Travel Clothing
entries.summary: Loose, protective travel clothing designed for heat, sun, sand, dry wind, and long journeys through open desert.

entries.name: Disguise Clothes
entries.summary: Plain adaptable garments chosen to support changes of social presentation without constituting a disguise by themselves.

entries.name: Dockworker's Clothes
entries.summary: Sturdy working clothes for hauling cargo, handling ropes, loading ships, and enduring wet, crowded docks.

entries.name: Fine Ball Attire
entries.summary: Elegant formal clothing suited for dances, noble celebrations, court gatherings, and other occasions where appearance carries social weight.

entries.name: Frontier Travel Clothes
entries.summary: Hard-wearing clothes for rough roads, border settlements, camps, and places where comfort matters less than durability.

entries.name: Hunter's Clothes
entries.summary: Durable field clothing suited for forests, traps, game trails, cold mornings, and quiet movement through brush.

entries.name: Hunter's Hood
entries.summary: A practical field hood that cuts glare and weather while breaking up the wearer’s outline in woodland terrain.

entries.name: Mage Attire
entries.summary: Layered spellcaster clothing arranged to leave hands, foci, and ritual movement unobstructed while clearly marking the wearer as a working mage.

entries.name: Merchant's Fine Clothes
entries.summary: Respectable, well-made clothing that signals prosperity without claiming noble rank, suitable for guild halls, counting houses, and trade meetings.

entries.name: Military Uniform
entries.summary: A regulation martial uniform suited for army, militia, border duty, or formal training, announcing discipline without functioning as armor.

entries.name: Mining Workwear
entries.summary: Rugged work clothing made for tunnels, stone dust, mud, darkness, and heavy labor below ground.

entries.name: Monastic Cowl
entries.summary: A plain monastic cowl worn for prayer, study, weather, and the quiet anonymity of disciplined communal life.

entries.name: Monastic Robes
entries.summary: Simple robes for disciplined religious or contemplative life, made for routine, study, service, and restraint rather than display.

entries.name: Mountain Travel Cloak
entries.summary: A wind-resistant cloak cut for high passes and exposed mountain roads, heavy enough to blunt cold without becoming armor.

entries.name: Mountain Travel Clothes
entries.summary: Sturdy layered clothing suited for steep paths, cold mornings, rough stone, high passes, and mountain settlements.

entries.name: Mourning Clothes
entries.summary: Somber formal clothing suited for funerals, memorials, grief rites, and households marked by recent loss.

entries.name: Noble's Attire
entries.summary: Fine court clothing whose cut, fabric, and finish signal noble upbringing, wealth, and familiarity with high household expectations.

entries.name: Noble's Court Cloak
entries.summary: A formal noble cloak of quality fabric and restrained ornament, worn to complete court dress without serving as proof of rank by itself.

entries.name: Nomad Caravan Clothes
entries.summary: Layered mobile clothing suited for caravan life, long roads, dust, shifting weather, and camps that move with their people.

entries.name: Palace Servant Livery
entries.summary: Formal high-household livery, better made than common service clothes but unmistakably identifying the wearer as palace or noble staff.

entries.name: Peasant's Work Clothes
entries.summary: Rough, durable clothing made for fields, barns, muddy roads, and hard physical labor.

entries.name: Performer Costume
entries.summary: Expressive stage clothing suited for taverns, festivals, dances, street performance, and dramatic entrances where being noticed is part of the work.

entries.name: Raincloak
entries.summary: A waxed raincloak made to shed persistent rain and road spray while remaining practical for travel.

entries.name: Raincloak Travel Clothes
entries.summary: Practical travel clothing for wet roads, muddy villages, river crossings, and long days in miserable weather.

entries.name: Ranger's Garb
entries.summary: Practical outdoor clothing suited for scouts, hunters, border runners, forest paths, and long travel through wild country.

entries.name: Ranger's Hooded Cloak
entries.summary: A weathered hooded cloak that offers concealment from rain, wind, and casual observation on wooded roads.

entries.name: Refugee Rags
entries.summary: Worn, patched, mismatched clothing kept serviceable by necessity, suggesting flight, poverty, loss, or survival after better things were left behind.

entries.name: Runed Command Mantle
entries.summary: A dark, broad-shouldered mantle lined with faded silver cloth and bordered by command runes representing the order’s ancient oath, Crown charter, fortress wards, and duty to the Argent territories. It was made to be worn by a recognized First Fang during formal command and major rites. Without lawful recognition it remains ceremonial regalia rather than proof of office.

entries.name: Sailor's Clothes
entries.summary: Hard-wearing shipboard clothing suited for wet decks, rope work, salt air, wind, and repeated rough handling.

entries.name: Scholar's Robes
entries.summary: Comfortable scholarly clothing suited for libraries, archives, tutors, academies, and long hours with ink, paper, and books.

entries.name: Servant's Uniform
entries.summary: A clean, modest household uniform suited for kitchens, halls, estates, and service work where staff are expected to be present but unobtrusive.

entries.name: Smith's Workwear
entries.summary: Heavy forge workwear with a protective apron, built for soot, sparks, tools, hot metal, and long hours beside an anvil.

entries.name: Stealth Clothing
entries.summary: Dark, close-fitting clothing chosen for quiet movement, rooftops, hidden paths, and situations where loose or bright fabric would betray the wearer.

entries.name: Stealth Hood
entries.summary: A close-fitting dark hood that reduces glare and visual recognition without providing meaningful armor.

entries.name: Street Urchin Clothes
entries.summary: Layered, patched street clothing with useful pockets and easy movement through alleys, markets, and crowded districts.

entries.name: Temple Cowl
entries.summary: A simple temple cowl associated with prayer, service, and formal religious observance rather than worldly rank.

entries.name: Temple Vestments
entries.summary: Religious vestments suited for temple service, rites, blessings, shrine duties, and public observance of sacred office.

entries.name: Traveler's Outfit
entries.summary: Practical road clothing suited for inns, wagons, changing weather, and ordinary long-distance travel.

entries.name: Traveler's Road Cloak
entries.summary: A sturdy road cloak made for wind, dust, rain, and the repeated wear of long journeys.

entries.name: Village Festival Clothes
entries.summary: A cherished set of festive village clothing with modest decoration, worn for dances, seasonal rites, gatherings, and local celebrations.

entries.name: Aurel
entries.summary: The standard coin of Eldaven, used for all trade from market food and lodging to tools, weapons, horses, professional fees, noble expenses, military contracts, and major purchases. All prices, wages, rewards, loot, debts, and payments are counted in whole Aurels only.

entries.name: Barracks Muster Token
entries.summary: A stamped token granting entry to a scheduled military muster or barracks assembly.

entries.name: Concealed Package
entries.summary: A carefully wrapped package prepared to pass without attracting attention; its contents are not obvious from the outside.

entries.name: Court Attendance Token
entries.summary: A minor court token used by guards and attendants to confirm expected access or attendance.

entries.name: Crownspire Lesson Token
entries.summary: A small academy token issued for a supervised lesson, appointment, or controlled instructional access.

entries.name: Cult Investigation Dossier
entries.summary: A compiled investigation dossier containing notes, names, leads, and evidence concerning suspected cult activity.

entries.name: Debt Contract Copy
entries.summary: A copied debt contract recording terms, witnesses, obligations, and the parties named in the agreement.

entries.name: Emergency Contact Cipher
entries.summary: A compact cipher reference intended to let its holder recognize or produce an emergency contact signal.

entries.name: Forged Dock Permit
entries.summary: A false or altered permit prepared to provide plausible access to controlled dock facilities.

entries.name: Forged Id
entries.summary: A carefully prepared false identity document meant to survive casual inspection.

entries.name: Founder's Hilt
entries.summary: The original hilt of the Fenrisard-Argenwald Founder’s weapon, formed around a dark metal tang cradle with silver runes running through its guard and grip. Its fittings are designed to receive the Argent Heart and the reunited blade sections. Alone it is an irreplaceable relic rather than a usable weapon, and possession confers no title or command authority.

entries.name: Greyhaven Local Notice
entries.summary: A rough written notice from Greyhaven's local board, intended for public posting or ordinary village circulation.

entries.name: Guild Quarter Contract
entries.summary: A signed contract associated with Highcourt Armathen's Guild Quarter, recording agreed work, service, or commercial terms.

entries.name: Lantern Witness Slip
entries.summary: A narrow witness slip naming the bearer as expected for a formal testimony, verification, or recorded appearance.

entries.name: Letter From N
entries.summary: A sealed letter from someone identifying themselves only as N, written to be opened and read by its intended recipient.

entries.name: Lower Argentsteel Blade
entries.summary: The lower section of the broken Founder’s blade, including the reinforced base that once joined the weapon’s hilt. Its silver-gray surface holds layered rune channels interrupted by the ancient break. The fragment is too heavy and dangerously unbalanced to use safely on its own, but its surviving structure can still be reunited through the lost Argentsteel joining process.

entries.name: Merchant's Assistant Papers
entries.summary: Official papers identifying the bearer as an assistant or representative attached to a merchant concern.

entries.name: Sealed Omen Slip
entries.summary: A sealed slip containing an omen, symbolic reading, or formal divinatory message intended for later inspection.

entries.name: Sealed Royal Summons
entries.summary: A folded parchment sealed with crown authority and intended to compel or formally request the named recipient’s attendance.

entries.name: Upper Argentsteel Blade
entries.summary: The forward section and point of the broken Founder’s blade, preserved despite deep scars left by the Sundering. Dormant rune lines remain visible beneath the Argentsteel whenever magic passes nearby. It cannot serve as a practical weapon alone and must be precisely aligned with the lower section before the blade’s original structure can be restored.

entries.name: Valmere Invitation Letter
entries.summary: A carefully worded invitation bearing House Valmere identification and intended for a named recipient.

entries.name: Buckler Shield
entries.summary: A small hand shield suited for duelists, scouts, light fighters, and anyone who wants defense without giving up too much speed.

entries.name: Heater Shield
entries.summary: A knightly shield with strong body coverage and a shape suited for disciplined melee defense. Often associated with soldiers, guards, nobles, and trained protectors.

entries.name: Kite Shield
entries.summary: A long shield offering broad protection for mounted or foot combat. It is well suited for defensive fighters, bodyguards, and warriors who expect arrows, spears, and hard charges.

entries.name: Round Shield
entries.summary: A practical round shield used by warriors, guards, hunters, raiders, and frontier fighters. Balanced between defense, movement, and shield-bash utility.

entries.name: Small Shield
entries.summary: A compact shield suited for travel, skirmishing, light defense, and quick repositioning. Easier to carry than larger shields and still much better than bare forearms.

entries.name: Tower Shield
entries.summary: A massive shield built for cover, formation defense, chokepoints, and protecting allies from devastating attacks. Heavy, awkward, and almost a portable wall in trained hands.

entries.name: Arbalest
entries.summary: A heavy winched crossbow with punishing force, slow reload, and terrifying performance against armor at prepared range.

entries.name: Bardiche
entries.summary: A broad axe-bladed polearm built for powerful cuts, hooking pressure, and control at battlefield reach.

entries.name: Bastard Sword
entries.summary: A hand-and-a-half sword that bridges agile one-handed cuts and stronger two-handed leverage.

entries.name: Battle Axe
entries.summary: A martial axe designed to split shields, hook defenses, and deliver brutal chopping force. It has none of a court blade's elegance and all of a battlefield's honesty.

entries.name: Battle Staff
entries.summary: A reinforced fighting staff made for battlefield pressure, guards, sweeps, and armored strikes.

entries.name: Bearded Axe
entries.summary: A hooked axe with a lowered blade edge, useful for cuts, pulls, shield work, and close control.

entries.name: Billhook
entries.summary: A hooked pole weapon adapted from forestry tools, useful for pulling shields, catching limbs, and dragging riders down.

entries.name: Bo Staff
entries.summary: A long balanced staff focused on reach, rhythm, and clean strikes without exceeding heavier reinforced staves.

entries.name: Boar Spear
entries.summary: A sturdy hunting spear with lugs to stop a charging beast from driving up the shaft.

entries.name: Cavalry Lance
entries.summary: A standard mounted battlefield lance built for disciplined couched charges and shock impact.

entries.name: Cestus
entries.summary: A reinforced fighting glove with metal bands that turns close punches into punishing armored strikes.

entries.name: Chakram
entries.summary: A flat razor-edged throwing ring balanced for fast ranged cuts and practiced return lines.

entries.name: Claw Gauntlets
entries.summary: Reinforced gauntlets with short clawed edges for raking strikes during grapples and close body control.

entries.name: Claymore
entries.summary: A large two-handed sword with reach and presence, comparable in force to other great blades rather than superior to them.

entries.name: Compound Bow
entries.summary: An engineered bow using compact mechanical advantage to hold tension efficiently without outclassing a trained longbow.

entries.name: Court Sabre
entries.summary: A curved dueling blade favored in noble salons, military dress, and fast formal swordplay.

entries.name: Crossbow
entries.summary: A mechanical ranged weapon that stores force for a prepared shot. Favored by guards, hunters, militias, ambushers, and anyone who values aim and timing over draw strength.

entries.name: Cudgel
entries.summary: A short hardwood club suited for tavern violence, guard duty, and desperate close defense.

entries.name: Dart Set
entries.summary: A set of small balanced darts used for distraction, poison delivery, target practice, and quick close-range throws.

entries.name: Dirk
entries.summary: A long fighting dagger useful for close defense, camp work, and finishing thrusts in cramped spaces.

entries.name: Estoc
entries.summary: A stiff thrusting sword designed to drive precise points into gaps in armor and guarded defenses.

entries.name: Fauchard
entries.summary: A long polearm with a forward-curving blade suited for hooking, slashing, and controlling reach from outside sword range.

entries.name: Flail
entries.summary: A chain-linked striking weapon used to wrap around shields, punish guarded enemies, and deliver unpredictable impact. Dangerous to the wielder without training, and worse for the enemy with it.

entries.name: Glaive
entries.summary: A long pole blade suited for sweeping cuts and re.

entries.name: Great Axe
entries.summary: A heavy two-handed axe built for overwhelming force, shield-breaking swings, and terrifying execution blows. It is not subtle, but few things that survive it care about subtlety.

entries.name: Greatsword
entries.summary: A large two-handed sword built for reach, weight, and decisive cutting force. It is difficult to hide, exhausting to use poorly, and terrifying when carried by someone trained to let momentum speak.

entries.name: Halberd
entries.summary: A long battlefield weapon combining axe blade, spear point, and hook. It controls space, threatens riders, punishes shields, and belongs to someone who thinks in reach and arcs.

entries.name: Hand Axe
entries.summary: A small axe useful for chopping wood, close combat, throwing, and rough travel. Practical enough for a frontier pack and dangerous enough for a battlefield.

entries.name: Hand Crossbow
entries.summary: A compact crossbow suited for concealed shots, close-range ambushes, off-hand use, and situations where a full bow would be too obvious.

entries.name: Hatchet
entries.summary: A small chopping axe that doubles as a crude sidearm, useful but limited in reach and stopping power.

entries.name: Heavy Crossbow
entries.summary: A reinforced crossbow built for heavy bolts, armor-piercing shots, and braced battlefield use.

entries.name: Heavy War Lance
entries.summary: A reinforced heavy lance made for mounted shock, armor-breaking charges, and brutal first impact.

entries.name: Hunting Bow
entries.summary: A simple practical bow for woodsmen, scouts, and hunters who value quiet handling and familiar draw weight.

entries.name: Hunting Sling
entries.summary: A compact leather sling sized for clean hunting shots at birds, rabbits, and other small game.

entries.name: Ironwood Staff
entries.summary: A dense dark-wood staff balanced for guards, sweeps, leverage, and hard two-handed strikes.

entries.name: Javelin
entries.summary: A light spear balanced for throwing before closing into melee or breaking an enemy approach.

entries.name: Jousting Lance
entries.summary: A tournament-focused lance heavier than a practice weapon but less lethal than a true war lance.

entries.name: Knightly Lance
entries.summary: A disciplined mounted weapon built for trained charges, battlefield shock, and controlled reach from horseback.

entries.name: Knuckles
entries.summary: A set of metal knuckles or reinforced hand wraps used to make punches hit harder without abandoning close-quarters brawling. Simple, ugly, and effective.

entries.name: Kodachi
entries.summary: A short curved single-edged blade suited for quick close cuts, confined spaces, and practical sidearm use.

entries.name: Lead-Shot Sling
entries.summary: A war sling intended for cast lead shot, delivering compact armor-bruising impact at surprising range.

entries.name: Light Crossbow
entries.summary: A lighter crossbow built for patrols, scouts, and hunters who need easier carry and faster handling than a heavy battlefield frame.

entries.name: Light Lance
entries.summary: A lighter mounted lance suited for scouts, couriers, skirmish cavalry, and fast charges.

entries.name: Long Spear
entries.summary: A longer battlefield spear that emphasizes reach, bracing, and keeping dangerous enemies at distance.

entries.name: Longbow
entries.summary: A powerful bow suited for battlefield range, hunting large game, and precise long-distance shots. It rewards strength, breath, training, and patience.

entries.name: Longsword
entries.summary: A balanced longsword suited for guards, soldiers, nobles, duelists, and adventurers. It is versatile enough for battlefield use and refined enough for formal training.

entries.name: Mace
entries.summary: A heavy single-handed bludgeon designed to crush armor and bone alike, bypassing the protection that turns edged weapons aside.

entries.name: Mage Staff
entries.summary: A staff designed as a magical focus and walking implement, suited for channeling mana through deliberate gestures and stable posture. It favors steady casting, ritual positioning, and controlled output over quick portability. Less a sidearm than a declaration that the wielder expects magic to answer.

entries.name: Main-Gauche
entries.summary: A parrying dagger used beside a precision blade to catch, bind, and answer enemy steel.

entries.name: Maul
entries.summary: A two-handed crushing weapon that sacrifices speed for overwhelming impact and armor-breaking force.

entries.name: Odachi
entries.summary: An exceptionally long two-handed curved sword built for reach, sweeping cuts, and committed battlefield strikes.

entries.name: Parrying Sword
entries.summary: A narrow defensive blade used to bind, deflect, and answer with precise counter-thrusts.

entries.name: Partisan
entries.summary: A spear-like polearm with side lugs that supports thrusting, binding, and defensive reach control.

entries.name: Pike
entries.summary: An extremely long formation spear meant to stop charges, dominate lanes, and punish enemies before they close.

entries.name: Quarterstaff
entries.summary: A sturdy two-handed staff useful for travel, defense, balance, and disciplined combat. Favored by monks, travelers, villagers, temple students, and mages who prefer a practical implement over a blade.

entries.name: Rapier
entries.summary: A slender thrusting blade suited for precision, dueling, courtly defense, and elegant violence. Favored by nobles, duelists, agents, and anyone who prefers timing over brute force.

entries.name: Recurve Bow
entries.summary: A compact, recurved bow suited for hunting, scouting, mounted use, and mobile skirmishing. It offers stronger draw and better range than a simple shortbow while remaining easier to carry and handle than a full longbow.

entries.name: Repeating Crossbow
entries.summary: A mechanism-fed crossbow that trades raw impact for faster follow-up shots and sustained pressure.

entries.name: Sap Gloves
entries.summary: Weighted gloves designed to make close punches land harder while keeping the hands free.

entries.name: Shepherd's Sling
entries.summary: A plain cord sling used by herders, villagers, and scouts for cheap, portable ranged defense.

entries.name: Short Spear
entries.summary: A compact thrusting spear suited for guards, hunters, and close formation work in tight spaces.

entries.name: Short Sword
entries.summary: A compact blade suited for guards, scouts, close quarters, narrow alleys, ship decks, and practical sidearm use. Easier to carry than a longsword and more reliable than a knife in a real fight.

entries.name: Shortbow
entries.summary: A compact bow suited for hunters, scouts, mounted riders, and travelers who need a ranged weapon that is easier to carry than a longbow.

entries.name: Shuriken
entries.summary: Small balanced throwing blades used for distraction, harassment, and quick close-range ranged attacks.

entries.name: Smallsword
entries.summary: A light thrusting blade suited for formal duels, quick footwork, and precise courtly violence.

entries.name: Spear
entries.summary: A simple, reliable thrusting weapon with reach enough to keep danger at bay. Favored by guards, soldiers, hunters, villagers, and anyone who understands the value of not letting claws get close.

entries.name: Spiked Gauntlets
entries.summary: Heavy fighting gauntlets fitted with short spikes for brutal punches, grapples, and close pressure.

entries.name: Staff Sling
entries.summary: A sling mounted to a staff, trading speed and convenience for greater leverage and heavier projectiles.

entries.name: Steel Dagger
entries.summary: A sharp steel dagger useful as a sidearm, tool, concealed weapon, or last resort. Small blades are rarely honorable, but they are often close enough when honor is not.

entries.name: Stiletto
entries.summary: A narrow thrusting dagger designed for precision and concealment rather than broad cutting force.

entries.name: Stone Sling
entries.summary: A plain cord sling for common stones, easy to carry and dangerous only in trained hands.

entries.name: Tachi
entries.summary: A curved single-edged sword suited for decisive cuts, mobile fighting, and disciplined two-handed technique.

entries.name: The Argent Vow
entries.summary: A restored Argentsteel sword built around the Argent Heart, with the two surviving blade sections joined to the Founder's Hilt. In the rites of the Runed Argent Fang it is called the Princeps’ Fang, while histories of the Sundering remember it as Oath Unbroken. Its runes adapt to the wielder’s established technique and can carry any Arcana they already possess through the blade without granting an affinity they lack. During the Sundering, its divided ward pattern held two converging fronts long enough for civilians and wounded defenders to escape, even as the strain broke the original blade into two sections. While equipped, its restored runes allow the wielder to invoke Oath Unbroken.

entries.name: Throwing Axe
entries.summary: A compact axe weighted to rotate predictably when thrown while remaining useful at close range.

entries.name: Throwing Knife
entries.summary: A narrow balanced blade made for accurate throwing at short to moderate range.

entries.name: Tournament Lance
entries.summary: A blunted lance made for formal lists, mounted trials, and controlled tournament impact rather than battlefield lethality.

entries.name: Twin Daggers
entries.summary: A matched pair of daggers suited for quick hands, close-range pressure, hidden angles, and twin-weapon fighting. Favored by rogues, duelists, assassins, street survivors, and anyone who dislikes leaving one hand idle.

entries.name: War Axe
entries.summary: A dedicated fighting axe balanced for armor-breaking chops and battlefield durability.

entries.name: War Bow
entries.summary: A heavy battlefield bow that rewards strength, training, and repeated practice over convenience.

entries.name: War Sling
entries.summary: A heavier sling built for battlefield bullets and armor-bruising impact at surprising range.

entries.name: War Staff
entries.summary: A reinforced staff capped for battle, built to withstand hard guards, sweeps, and repeated armored contact.

entries.name: Warhammer
entries.summary: A martial hammer designed to crack armor, break guards, stagger enemies, and turn defensive confidence into ringing impact.

entries.name: Weighted Handwraps
entries.summary: Weighted fighting wraps that harden punches while leaving the hands flexible for grappling and close control.

entries.name: Winged Spear
entries.summary: A spear with side wings for control, binding, and preventing over-penetration during disciplined thrusts.

entries.name: Wooden Club
entries.summary: A crude wooden club, simple enough for anyone to swing but dangerous in strong hands. It is the weapon of peasants, thugs, desperate travelers, and anyone who found violence before they found coin.
